height.doc: Standing height to the top of the head.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

biped_heavy.doc:
biped_heavy -- the tank: wide, upright, shoulders far wider than the hips,
short thick legs, a small head sunk between the shoulders. The silhouette is
a block with a head; nothing about it is lean.

height.doc: Standing height to the top of the head.

torso_length.doc: Hip to neck, along the leaning spine.

lean.doc: Forward pitch of the torso, radians.

arms.doc: Short arms held forward, or none.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

biped_lean.doc:
biped_lean -- a lean two-legged runner: long legs, narrow torso, a low
forward lean, small head out front. The lean is the silhouette: the torso is
pitched forward so the profile reads as a diagonal line, not a post.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

blob.doc:
blob -- a slime: a squashed sphere with a few lumps, a glowing core, no
limbs. The rig is four bones (root, core, top, front, back) so it can
squash, stretch and ooze.

bolt.doc: bolt -- an arrow: shaft, iron head, pale fletching. Points along +Z.

height.doc: Plinth to the top of the drum.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

cannon.doc:
cannon -- the mortar: a squat stone drum with a bronze barrel pitched at the
sky, iron bands, a pile of shot beside it. Squat on purpose: height is at
most 1.2 × width, so the thing that hits an area looks like it lobs.

height.doc: Plinth to the tip of the main crystal.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

crystal_emitter.doc:
crystal_emitter -- the frost shrine: a blue-grey pedestal with a cluster of
glowing crystals. The crystals are the visible emitter the slow tower's
silhouette rule demands, and they are the glow material so they read from
any angle.

height.doc: Top of the bell above the ground, including hover_height.

hover_height.doc: Gap between the ground and the lowest tendril.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

hover.doc:
hover -- a floating creature: a bell (jellyfish) or a balloon body with
tendrils hanging below, no legs, clear of the ground by `hover_height`.
The rig is root/body/bell/tendrils; hover_bob drives Idle and Walk.

height.doc: Height to the top of the shell.

shell_ratio.doc: How much of the body the shell covers.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

insect.doc:
insect -- the swarm creep: a beetle. Low, wide, longer than tall, six (or
more) legs, a shell over most of the body, mandibles. Small on purpose:
the archetype ships in numbers and reads as a texture of moving dots.

stretch.doc: Length along the flight, as a multiple of the radius.

orb.doc:
orb -- a glowing core with a darker rim round its flight axis: the frost
bolt when stretched, a hit burst when round.

flutes.doc: Vertical grooves; 0 for a plain shaft.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

pillar.doc:
pillar -- a plain column with a capital: the neutral tower body for anything
that is not a keep, a mortar or a shrine. What sits on top comes from the
part library (a crystal cluster, a banner, an emissive ring).

height.doc: Standing height to the top of the back, in tiles.

head_size.doc: Head scale relative to the body radius.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

quadruped.doc:
quadruped -- a four-legged runner. Long body, low head out front, tail up.
The runner archetype's silhouette rule is "lean, forward-leaning, a
horizontal line", so the body is a capsule longer than it is tall, the legs
are thin, and the head sits below the shoulder line.

shell.doc: shell -- a cannonball. An iron sphere, nothing else; it reads as a dot.

size.doc: Tiles per side: 1 for a lane tile, 2 for a tower footprint.

tile_flat.doc:
tile_flat -- a `size` × `size` slab, 2 cm thick: a lane tile at 1, a tower
footprint at 2 (the placement cursor). Colour comes from the palette role.

rune.doc: The glyph raised on the tile.

height.doc: How far the glyph stands above the slab.

size.doc: Tiles per side: 1 for a zone marker, 2 for a tower footprint.

tile_marker.doc:
tile_marker -- a slab with a raised glyph: an arrow for the spawn seam, a
ring for the exit seam, a cross for a refused footprint, a chevron for the
leak marker. The glyph is the glow material so it reads on any turf. At
`size` 2 the slab and the glyph cover a tower's footprint.

height.doc: Plinth to parapet, in the unit frame; x2 at the footprint. A spire or cone adds its own height, so a roofed level keeps this lower than the level below.

seed.doc: Extra entropy on top of the spec id, for variants of one plan.

turret_on_base.doc:
turret_on_base -- the guard tower: a tapering round keep on a square plinth
with a crenellated parapet. Tall and thin, as the single-target silhouette
rule asks: height is at least 2.5 × the keep's width.

imported.doc: An external model brought to the conventions by the import path. Parameters live under `import:`.

back_plates.doc: Three overlapping plates down the spine.

banner.doc:
A pole with a hanging banner in the accent colour, team-maskable. The
tier-3 / level-3 flourish.

club.doc: A wooden club with a knob, held in a hand, resting over the shoulder.

crystal_cluster.doc:
Five glowing crystal shards of different heights, leaning outward. The
level-3 part for the frost shrine; a tier-3 part for creeps.

crystal_shards.doc: Three small crystal shards, a lighter touch than the cluster.

emissive_trim.doc:
Six small glowing studs in a ring: the tier-3 emissive strip. Octahedra, not
spheres: 8 triangles each instead of 60, which is the difference between a
tier-3 creep fitting its budget and not.

extra_barrel.doc:
A second, shorter barrel beside the first, pitched the same way. The
level-3 part for the mortar.

gold_ring.doc:
A thin ring of trim around the body: gold at level 3, otherwise a dark
band. The cheapest level-3 signal there is; on a creep it is a belt at
the hips (or round a beetle's abdomen).

head_crest.doc:
A fin-like crest on the head, three thin fins fanning back. Accent colour
and team-maskable.

horns.doc: Two curved-looking horns (two cones each) sweeping up and out.

iron_bands.doc: Two iron bands around the body, a little apart.

roof_cone.doc: A conical wooden roof with a small finial. The level-2 part for the keep.

shoulder_plates.doc:
One armour plate over each shoulder, angled down and out. The tier-2 part
for heavy creeps. Plain boxes: at this size a bevel is invisible and costs
four times the triangles.

shoulder_spikes.doc:
A row of four spikes over each shoulder, angled outward and back. The tier-2
signature part for creeps: a silhouette change with no new body plan.

spike_row.doc: A row of five spikes along the spine, tallest in the middle.

spire.doc: A tall thin spire in the trim colour: gold at level 3.

tail_club.doc: A short thick tail ending in a spiked club.

tail_long.doc: A long tapering tail, two cones end to end, sweeping back and up.

biped_large.doc:
Sixteen bones for the heavy biped: spine chain, head, two per leg, three
per arm (upper arm, forearm, hand) so a club can swing from the hand.

biped_small.doc:
Sixteen bones for the lean biped: spine chain, head, a two-bone tail, two
bones per leg and two per arm. Arms have no hand bone; the forearm ends at
the hand joint.

blob.doc:
Five bones: root, a core the body hangs from, and top/front/back handles
for squash, stretch and ooze.

hover.doc:
Four bones: root, body (the skirt), bell (the head and eyes), tendrils.
hover_bob moves the root; the bell and tendrils lag it.

quadruped.doc:
Sixteen bones: root, a three-bone spine (hips, spine, chest), neck and head,
two bones per leg, a two-bone tail. Legs are FK; the walk generator plants
the feet arithmetically rather than through an IK solver, which keeps the
clip a pure function of its parameters (and IK constraints do not survive a
glTF export anyway).

turret.doc:
Four bones for every tower: root, base (the plinth and body), turret (the
top, which recoils, pulses or flashes), muzzle (where the projectile
leaves; the `muzzle` attachment follows it).

build_up.doc:
A tower is built: it rises from the ground in two stages -- the base first,
then the turret pops up with a small overshoot -- and ends at rest.

duration.doc: Seconds from the last step to lying still.

impact.doc: Normalised time the body hits the ground; the `impact` marker.

sink.doc: How far below ground the root ends, so a corpse can settle into the turf.

drop.doc: How far the body drops as the legs fold, as a fraction of the model height.

roll.doc: How far it rolls onto its side after the impact, radians.

collapse_forward.doc:
The creature's legs fold and the body drops, it pitches forward a little,
hits the ground at the impact marker and rolls onto its side. The last frame
is held by the client as the corpse. Works on any rig with a root; uses
legs, head and tail when present. The pitch is small on purpose: the root is
at the feet, so a large pitch there stands the model on its nose.

impact.doc: When the pieces hit the ground; the `impact` marker.

crumble.doc:
The model shivers, then sinks and shrinks into the ground as if crumbling.
Root-only, so it fits any rig: a blob's death, a tower's sale.

stride.doc: Tiles per cycle if used as Walk.

hover_bob.doc:
A floating bob: the root rises and falls, the bell squashes at the bottom
of the bob, the tendrils lag. As Walk it adds a forward tilt.

idle_breathe.doc:
A breath: the chest (or whatever bone is nearest a chest) rises and falls
once per cycle, the head nods a little late, and nothing else moves. Works
on any rig that has a root; uses chest/neck/head when they exist.

fire.doc: When the pulse peaks; the `fire` marker.

pulse.doc:
A pulse: the turret (or the whole model) swells to the fire marker and
relaxes. The frost shrine's attack, and a plain Idle for towers when used
as a loop generator elsewhere.

overshoot.doc: How far past full size the pop goes before settling.

depth.doc: Start depth below ground, as a fraction of the model's own height.

land.doc: Normalised time the feet touch down; the `land` marker.

rise_from_ground.doc:
The model rises out of the ground and pops to full size with a small
overshoot. Root-only, so it works on every rig. The final frame is the rest
pose, so the client can crossfade into Idle or Walk with no jump. `depth` is
a fraction of the height and is resolved by the builder, which knows it.

stride.doc: Tiles per cycle if the creature moved.

cadence.doc: Cycles per second: fast, an insect.

scuttle.doc:
An insect scuttle: legs alternate in a tripod gait (l1, l3, r2 together),
the body sways side to side and the head twitches. Fast and small.

sell_sink.doc:
A tower is sold: it sinks into the ground, spinning a little, and ends
below the turf at zero scale.

kick.doc: How far the turret drops and rocks back, in tiles.

fire.doc: When the shot leaves; the `fire` marker.

turret_recoil.doc:
A shot: the turret snaps back and down at the fire marker and eases home.
The muzzle bone flares (scales) for two frames.

upgrade_flash.doc:
An upgrade lands: the whole model squashes and pops to full size with an
overshoot, then rests. Plays on the NEW level's model.

stride.doc: Tiles per cycle if the creature moved; the client divides speed by this.

cadence.doc: Cycles per second at natural speed.

walk_biped.doc:
A two-legged walk in place: legs alternate, knees fold on the forward
swing, arms counter-swing, the body bobs twice a cycle and leans into it.

stride.doc: Tiles covered per cycle if the creature moved; the client divides speed by this.

cadence.doc: Cycles per second at the creature's natural speed.

bob.doc: Body rise per step, in tiles.

walk_quadruped.doc:
A four-legged walk cycle in place: thighs swing fore and aft, shins fold on
the forward swing so the foot clears the ground, the body bobs twice a
cycle, the head counter-nods and the tail wags. One cycle is two steps of
each leg. The `stride` parameter is not used by the clip itself -- it is
recorded so the client can scale the loop to the creature's speed.
